- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to avoid missing downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the immediate next period; apply a 1–2 day lag correction or dampen the peak.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; introduce a “sentiment pivot” rule to reduce forecast slope after sentiment reversal.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply a “first 7 days” bias correction downward by 1–2%.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days below 70), model tends to ignore it; apply a “reversion buffer” to cap forecasts above 70–72.
- When sentiment is high but price drops sharply (e.g., 5–10% in 3 days), model often fails to anticipate; add a “sentiment-impact” multiplier to reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day of negative sentiment.
